description: Hi! I’m a high school student from Azerbaijan interested in AI, software development, space exploration, and STEM. I enjoy turning ideas into interactive projects and using AI-assisted coding to prototype quickly. For this challenge, I want to build an engaging Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer. I’m looking for teammates interested in programming, space, game design, UI/UX, AI/data, or storytelling.
summary: SUPER ASTRO is an interactive 3D Mars outpost survival and systems engineering simulator designed for students ages 8–14. Addressing the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge, it transforms complex spacecraft engineering trade-offs into a tangible, Sol-by-Sol command experience at Gale Crater. Players manage a 4-astronaut habitat by balancing competing demands across solar power, battery storage, closed-loop life support (O2 and water recovery), hydroponic food production, and a hydrogen-rich water-wall radiation shield. Grounded in real NASA Curiosity (REMS/RAD) and ISS (ECLSS) benchmarks, SUPER ASTRO teaches young learners how every engineering decision carries real-world consequences.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & WHY IT MATTERS:

Space-themed STEM content often oversimplifies mission engineering or overwhelms young students with dry equations. SUPER ASTRO bridges this gap by placing students in the role of an Outpost Commander at Gale Crater, Mars. Each Martian day (Sol), players must keep a crew of four healthy by making real engineering trade-offs where boosting one system directly constrains another.

HOW IT WORKS (CORE ENGINEERING TRADE-OFFS):

1. Coupled Power & Water Routing: Players distribute 100% of available electrical power (generated by solar arrays and buffered by batteries) and route up to 90 Liters of water per Sol across three core systems:

- Life Support & O2 Loop: Mirrors NASA's ISS ECLSS, recovering 93–98% of wastewater and using electrolysis to generate breathable oxygen.

- Water-Wall Radiation Shield: Pumps water into a protective dome shell around the habitat. Because hydrogen-rich water absorbs energetic cosmic and solar particles, a fuller shield reduces crew radiation dose—but locks away water needed for crops and oxygen generation.

- Hydroponic Greenhouse & Thermal Control: Maintains cabin temperature against -62°C Martian nights and grows crew food reserves.

2. Interactive 3D WebGL Outpost: Built with Three.js, the 3D scene features geodesic habitat domes, a dynamic cyan water-shield shell, solar arrays, a greenhouse pod, a rover, and orbiting moons (Phobos and Deimos). The 3D base visually responds in real time to player allocations and weather events (dust storms, solar particle events, and emergency beacons). Clicking or hovering on 3D modules educates students on each subsystem's engineering function.

3. Dynamic Contingencies & NASA Science Debriefs: Players face realistic emergencies—Global Dust Storms, Solar Particle Events, ECLSS Filter Clogs, and Micro-Meteorite Impacts. After every decision, an interactive debrief explains "What happened?" alongside a bite-sized "NASA Science Fact."

4. Competitive Classroom Retention: A local Commander Leaderboard ranks runs by Sols Survived + Engineering Efficiency Score, encouraging students to test new strategies and replay.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED:

- Frontend & UI: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6 Modules), Tailwind CSS, Font Awesome, Google Fonts.

- 3D Graphics Engine: Three.js (WebGL procedural Martian terrain, lighting, particle systems, and OrbitControls).

- Audio Engine: Procedural Web Audio API synthesizer (100% royalty-free ambient space drone and UI sound effects).

- Storage: Browser localStorage for zero-login leaderboard persistence and custom mission patch logo support.
